original_question: For every positive integer n divisible by 4, does there exist an n x n Hadamard matrix (a matrix with entries in {+1,-1} and mutually orthogonal columns)?
target_in_paper: Conjecture 14 (Hadamard Conjecture) in Entry 6, stated in the final note after the discussion of Hadamard matrices. ([anmaillard.github.io](https://anmaillard.github.io/assets/pdf/publications/bandeira2025randomstrasse.pdf))
correct_elements: Your draft already captures almost all of the paper's official statement: the quantifier is over all positive integers n with 4 dividing n; the object sought is an n x n Hadamard matrix; and the defining property used in the nearby context is exactly that the matrix has entries in {+1,-1} and pairwise orthogonal columns. ([anmaillard.github.io](https://anmaillard.github.io/assets/pdf/publications/bandeira2025randomstrasse.pdf))
missing_details: The nearby definition makes explicit that orthogonality is with respect to the standard real inner product, since the paper immediately says that after scaling by 1/sqrt(n) the matrix is an orthogonal matrix. ([anmaillard.github.io](https://anmaillard.github.io/assets/pdf/publications/bandeira2025randomstrasse.pdf))

The paper presents this as a named conjecture, namely 'Conjecture 14 (Hadamard Conjecture),' rather than as an informal existence question. ([anmaillard.github.io](https://anmaillard.github.io/assets/pdf/publications/bandeira2025randomstrasse.pdf))
refined_question: Hadamard Conjecture: For every positive integer n with 4|n, does there exist an n x n matrix H with entries in {+1,-1} whose columns are pairwise orthogonal under the standard real inner product (equivalently, (1/sqrt(n))H is an orthogonal matrix)? ([anmaillard.github.io](https://anmaillard.github.io/assets/pdf/publications/bandeira2025randomstrasse.pdf))
equivalent_formulation: Equivalently, for every positive integer n with 4|n, does there exist H in {+1,-1}^{n x n} such that (1/sqrt(n))H is an orthogonal matrix? ([anmaillard.github.io](https://anmaillard.github.io/assets/pdf/publications/bandeira2025randomstrasse.pdf))
justification: In this paper, the relevant passage is not one of the main discrepancy questions but the final note of Entry 6: the authors first define a Hadamard matrix as a ±1 matrix whose columns are all orthogonal, explicitly noting the equivalent scaled-orthogonal formulation, and then state 'Conjecture 14 (Hadamard Conjecture): For any positive n a multiple of 4, there exists an n x n Hadamard matrix.' Your draft is therefore already very close and is targeting that exact statement. ([anmaillard.github.io](https://anmaillard.github.io/assets/pdf/publications/bandeira2025randomstrasse.pdf))
